title: The LLM critic on 50 experiments, and the gate that checks its objections against the numbers
request: Send the campaign's 50 bounded review tasks to a capable LLM critic and keep only cited, reviewed conclusions as durable memory. Later: make sure a critic's wrong objection never becomes memory or training data.
spec: make rd-campaign-review runs pending critic tasks (OPENAI_API_KEY from .env) and writes llm_review_memory.jsonl and LLM_REVIEW_REPORT.md; metrics in the result JSON stay authoritative. critic_gate.py recomputes each stage's recorded selection rule and marks a challenge that disputes a confirmed selection as contradicted; contradicted challenges are excluded from memory and from the SFT corpus.
plan: Give the critic one bounded task per experiment: the evidence bundle, the claims, and a required answer format (evidence, interpretation, decision, risks, smallest next test).
Run the 50 reviews and render the report; keep the model's challenges with an id and a severity.
When building the knowledge layer, read the critic's challenges against the recorded numbers before using them.
Write critic_gate.py: parse each stage's selection rule (tolerance, std penalty, acceptance margin) and recompute the choice from the recorded rows.
Drop contradicted challenges from memory and from the SFT builder; make the gate metric-aware when the expansion campaign added other metrics.

decisions.decision: The LLM critic may challenge and propose; it may not rewrite an observed metric or approve deployment.
decisions.why: The critic reads the same evidence a person reads and can be wrong; the numbers are measured by code.

decisions.decision: Store only cited conclusions, never free chat, as durable memory.
decisions.why: Memory that later trains a model must be checkable against a result file.

decisions.decision: Recompute the rule rather than ask a second model to judge the first.
decisions.why: Every stage records its rule beside the numbers it was applied to, so a deterministic recomputation settles the dispute.

change: dclab_rnd/llm_review.py and the review report and memory for model_building_50_v1; dclab_rnd/critic_gate.py with a per-experiment report; the SFT v3 builder and the evidence index read the gate's verdicts.

findings.defect: The critic reported selection-rule violations that do not exist.
findings.scenario: The feature ladder contains a recipe literally named `selected` (a feature-selection subset). On adult's feature stage (EXP-003) the critic read it as the recipe the rule selected and objected that 'selected' scored below raw despite the rule; the recorded rule had chosen raw. An earlier chat praised this as a real catch. Across the campaign, 10 of 157 challenges were of this kind.
findings.cause: A name collision between a recipe called selected and the rule's selected stage, and no step that recomputed the rule before trusting the objection.
findings.fix: critic_gate.py recomputes each stage's choice from the recorded rows and rule; a challenge that disputes a confirmed choice is marked contradicted and dropped (10 dropped, 147 kept).
findings.test: tests/test_knowledge_layer.py checks the gate; the SFT v3 manifest records contradicted_challenges_dropped 10.

findings.defect: The gate always recomputed on ROC-AUC with fixed tolerances.
findings.scenario: The fraud experiments (EXP-054, EXP-055) select on average precision with a 0.005 margin; the gate recomputed them on ROC-AUC and reported disagreement with recorded choices that hold when recomputed on average precision.
findings.cause: The metric, tolerance and margin were constants written for the binary campaign.
findings.fix: Read the primary metric, its direction (MAE, RMSE, log loss and Brier are lower-is-better), the tolerance, the std penalty and the acceptance margin from each result's recorded rule.
findings.test: tests/test_knowledge_layer.py; afterwards all 42 recomputable selections across 70 experiments are consistent.

measurements.name: critic review of 50 experiments
measurements.gate: Each review must cite the evidence and end with a decision and a falsifiable next experiment; no accuracy threshold.
measurements.result: 50 reviews by gpt-5.4-mini; confidence high on 4 and medium on 46; all 50 decisions withheld acceptance (do not accept, provisional, insufficient evidence or hold), most asking for repeated or nested CV and a decision-time audit.
measurements.next: Check each challenge against the recorded numbers before it becomes memory.

measurements.name: critic gate consistency
measurements.gate: Every recomputable selection must agree with the choice the result recorded.
measurements.result: 42 of 42 recomputable selections across 70 experiments consistent after the gate became metric-aware; 10 of 157 critic challenges contradicted.
measurements.next: Run the gate on every new campaign before make knowledge.

outcome: The critic's conservative reviews are kept as cited memory; its 10 checkably wrong objections are filtered out before they reach the evidence index or the SFT corpus.
lessons: A critic that sounds careful can still be wrong in a way code can check; recompute before you remember.
Never name an artefact after a role in the rule that judges it (a recipe called selected beside a selected stage).
A model that withholds acceptance on every experiment gives its value in specific challenges, not in its verdicts.
